gen-dafont-redux-gf-mochiy-pop-p-one: Wide-spaced and a little retro-geometric, Redux swoops into every curve. Mochiy Pop P One follows in sans-serif, big in the lowercase and strokes in lockstep, so a long page keeps a smooth, unfussy pace.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-montserrat-underline: Clean and contemporary up top, Redux shimmers faintly in weight across its widely spaced words. And Montserrat Underline brings hollow, oversized lowercase with curves that never pinch, which is the steadiest thing about the pair.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-mozilla-headline: Mozilla Headline brings big-bodied lowercase and a splayed c terminal beneath the heading. But Redux does its best work with that gentle weight modulation and wide spacing, while the body simply gets on with being friendly sans.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-mozilla-text: Wide, geometric, a touch of dip-pen flex. Mozilla Text reads as tall, bold-looking sans lowercase with flared terminals, so a long stretch of it feels dense, sturdy and easy to settle into.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-nata-sans: Redux sweeps a big entry stroke into every curve, with a brush-like hint of pressure. Nata Sans follows in plain sans with zero stroke contrast and open-mouthed curves, so a long page reads with technical-pen steadiness.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-nobile: Nobile keeps its caps close to the lowercase height. Its open, chalk-arc letter mouths make a long page read briskly beneath Redux, whose curves thin slightly at the tops.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-nokora: Nokora lays down a thick, dark stripe of lowercase. Its strongest quality is that weight against Redux, which sits at a comfortable midpoint between flat and dramatic strokes.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-kufi-arabic: Redux spaces its letters wide and swells its weight gradually. Under it, Noto Kufi Arabic offers an open c and caps barely above the lowercase, so the heading stretches out while the text stays quietly compact.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans: Noto Sans fills most of its letter height with lowercase and leaves the c wide open. Noto Sans is the pair's anchor, a sturdy, low-contrast partner for Redux, whose thin strokes are only slightly lighter than its thick ones.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-noto-sans-adlam: Redux leads with a faint but real thick-thin shift and wide, geometric spacing. But Noto Sans Adlam does the heavier lifting in sans text, keeping curve endings well apart and its c, s and z standing tall.
